claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I have one child - Alex. They're 19 and still studying, living at home with me. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 19 and still studying and living at home with you.

To help me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions:

**What type of education or training is Alex currently doing? For example, is it A-levels, further education at college, university, or an approved training course?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is doing A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! That's helpful information. A-levels at a sixth form college would typically count as approved education.

Now I need to ask:

**How many hours per week (if any) is Alex working in paid employment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't work - they're just focused on their studies at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you. Now I need to understand your own circumstances:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not actually sure about that - my living situation is a bit complicated at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand that living situations can sometimes be complicated. Let me ask this in a different way:

**Where are you currently residing most of the time - are you physically present in the UK, or are you living elsewhere?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into the specifics of where exactly I am right now - it's a bit of a complicated situation. Can we just say it's unclear at the moment?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand, and thank you for being honest about your situation.

Let me ask a few more questions to see if I can determine eligibility based on other factors:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, such as another parent or guardian?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Let me ask another important question:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't get any benefits in their own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to complete my assessment:

**Are you responsible for Alex's upkeep - meaning do you provide for their needs such as food, clothes, accommodation, and other living expenses?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely - I provide for all of Alex's needs, their food, clothes, everything they need really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I have enough information now to provide you with an assessment.

Based on what you've told me:

- **Alex is 19 years old** and doing A-levels at sixth form college, which would normally count as approved education or training
- **Alex is not working** 24 hours or more per week
- **Alex is not receiving benefits** in their own right
- **You are responsible for Alex's upkeep** and they live with you
- **No one else is claiming** Child Benefit for Alex

However, there is one critical factor that prevents me from determining definite eligibility:

**Your residence status is unclear.** One of the fundamental requirements for Child Benefit is that you normally live in the UK. Since you've indicated your living situation is complicated and unclear at the moment, I cannot definitively determine whether you meet this essential eligibility criterion.

If you were clearly residing in the UK, Alex would likely be eligible for Child Benefit as they're under 20 and in approved education. But without clarity on your UK residence status, I cannot make a definite assessment.
